Shared Authenticator contract — a new Authenticator functional interface (Optional<AuthResult> authenticate(HttpServletRequest)) is now implemented by both AuthFilter and AuthFilterChain, so every existing filter (SAML / OAuth / JWT / API-key / bearer) is reusable verbatim at the resource layer. RestAuthenticator.of(Authenticator) adapts any of them. AuthResult merge modes — AuthResult gains an immutable merge mode: of(...) = ADD (union roles, principal required — unchanged), ofRoles(...) = roles-only ADD (null principal — keeps the inherited identity), replacing(...) = REPLACE (swap identity outright). The existing of(...) factories and behavior are preserved (backward compatible). Registration & DI — resolved per RestContext with precedence registered bean › @Bean method › @Rest(authenticator=...) › RestServlet.createAuthenticator(BeanStore). Both Authenticator-into-RestAuthenticator and RestAuthenticator-into-resource injection work through the bean store. Inheritance & folding — unlike guards, authenticators inherit down the child-resource tree: a single root authenticator covers all descendants, which may augment (add roles), replace (swap identity), or opt out with @Rest(noInherit={"authenticator"}). @Rest(children = { ChildResource.class }) public class RootResource extends BasicRestServlet { @Bean public RestAuthenticator authenticator(AuthFilterChain chain) { return RestAuthenticator.of(chain); // covers root + all descendants } } See the new REST Authenticator — Resource-Level Authentication topic page.

Juneau 10.0 replaces Queryable's hand-rolled search/view/sort/paging code (ObjectSearcher/ObjectSorter/ObjectViewer/ObjectPaginator) with the shared BeanQuery engine, so one search language, one set of limits and one error model cover REST responses, DataTables server-side processing and SQL-backed queries. A new opt-in module also ships a DataTables server-side processing adapter plus browser-side helpers. Queryable on BeanQuery — the search / view / sort / position / limit / opts request parameters (bound by BeanQueryRequest) run against an InMemoryBeanQueryContext built from the response's row type (one context per element class, cached for the life of the converter; Map rows get a per-request context). Example: GET /people?search=age=$gte(18)&sort=name,age:desc&view=name,age&position=20&limit=10. Non-tabular results are returned unchanged. QueryableSettings — a bean-store-resolved per-resource bean (mirroring IntrospectableSettings) that tunes the context: defaultLimit (100), maxLimit (1000), allowRegex (on by default, allowRegex(false) opts out), regexTimeout, countPolicy, and the search-clause / sort-key / search-length / expression-depth caps. Unset settings keep the BeanQuery builder defaults. Counts — ?opts=counts=true adds X-BeanQuery-Total and X-BeanQuery-Matched response headers (each only when that count was computed). The body stays a bare list. Central error mapping — RestContext.convertThrowable maps BeanQuerySyntaxException to HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error: <CODE> header (BeanQueryRequest.ERROR_HEADER) and, with problem details on, a "code" member in the body; BeanQueryExecutionException maps to HTTP 500 with the fixed body Query execution failed. (the cause is logged, never sent to the client). The DataTables adapter uses the same contract (next bullet). juneau-console-datatables module (org.apache.juneau:juneau-console-datatables) — a new opt-in add-on (not bundled in juneau-distrib, mirroring the juneau-rest-server-management-logging precedent) with: DataTablesQuery (org.apache.juneau.console.datatables.adapter) — maps the DataTables server-side contract onto BeanQuery: DataTablesQuery.toBeanQuery(req, ctx) builds a BeanQuery from a DataTablesRequest (per-column search, order, paging, and a global search that expands to an $or of a per-SearchType leaf — $contains/$prefix/$eqic/$eq — over every searchable, resolvable column, not just text), and DataTablesQuery.run/runArrays execute it and map the result onto the DataTables envelope. The browser posts the draw state as JSON (not DataTables' default form-encoded request) through a new JuneauDataTables.ajax(url, extra?) helper in juneau-datatables.js, or the data-juneau-datatable-ajax auto-init attribute. A malformed request (unknown column, a maxSearchClauses/maxSortKeys cap exceeded, a bad search expression) raises BeanQuerySyntaxException, which the adapter does not catch: the central mapping answers HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error: <CODE> header and the message in the body, exactly like any other Queryable endpoint. JuneauDataTables.ajax installs an xhr.dt listener that shows that server message through DataTables' normal error path (the error.dt event, then DataTable.ext.errMode) instead of a generic "Ajax error"; other failed requests keep the DataTables default. An execution failure is HTTP 500 via the central BeanQueryExecutionException mapping. See DataTables. Views runtime server-mode tables now ride the same wire format. A juneau-console-views table with dataMode: "server" now gets serverSide: true and ajax: JuneauDataTables.ajax(url, {...}) (in juneau-views.js: buildOptions → buildServerAjax) instead of a hand-built GET config, so there is one wire format end to end. Breaking for existing server-mode endpoints: they must now be @RestPost methods taking @Content DataTablesRequest, not GET handlers reading query-string parameters. Column-scoped ribbon options now ride the JSON body as that column's search.value (ribbonColumnSearches), $and-merged with the user's own search on the same column (mergeColumnSearches) — fixing a bug where such filters were silently dropped. param:-scoped ribbon options (ribbonQueryParams) and the nested-table parent-scope param (applyNestedScope) stay URL query parameters, re-derived on every request through beforeSend. Client-mode tables are unchanged. A page must load juneau-datatables.js before juneau-views.js; otherwise server mode fails loudly (a warning) instead of silently falling back to GET. See DataTables. DataTablesResults<T> — the {draw,recordsTotal,recordsFiltered,data} (+ optional error) envelope bean, rendered by the negotiated serializer (no hardcoded JSON). Browser-side helpers — DataTablesColumns (generate columns:[…] from bean-property order + @Schema titles), DataTablesTable (build a DataTables-ready HTML5 Table DOM bean, with MarshallingContext overloads), and DataTablesMixin (serves a first-party juneau-datatables.js auto-init glue script). DataTables' own JS/CSS and jQuery remain caller-provided (not vendored — their license is not ASF category-A).
documents.s: Queryable rebuilt on the BeanQuery engine + juneau-console-datatables (new module)

documents.t: Juneau 10.0 adds two opt-in modules that give an admin-console-style resource a themeable CSS "chrome", an enum status/domain pill component, and (for FreeMarker consumers) macro-based composition — without pulling a template engine or the DataTables add-on into juneau-rest-server core. The two modules form an acyclic dependency chain (juneau-console → juneau-console-freemarker); a chrome-only consumer never drags in FreeMarker or DataTables transitively. juneau-console — ConsoleChromeMixin serves a dynamically themed chrome.css (the module's shipped structural stylesheet plus a :root block built from validated --jc-* theme tokens); Theme validates every token value through a normalize-then-accept-known-safe pipeline (reject C0/C1/DEL control chars → strip CSS comments → case-insensitively reject any url( production → match an allowlist grammar for colors/fonts/lengths/gradients) rather than a denylist, so a token value can never smuggle a url()-based injection. Color/font/length tokens sink only into non-URL-capable CSS properties; the sole URL-capable sink (background-image, for --jc-page-bg/--jc-avatar-bg) is unreachable via url() anyway since the grammar structurally excludes that production. The console logo is a static chrome.css constant, not a configurable token. The reusable enum pill/badge component (<span class="tag <domain> <value>">) is rendered by the <@tag domain=... value=.../> FreeMarker macro in the console base.ftlh (see Admin Console Chrome). Console theming is FTL-only: custom palettes are authored with <@theme>/<@token> (value= for leaves, alias= for live var() references). ThemePack, ThemeSettings, ThemePackSettings, ConsoleChromeMixin.Builder.pack(...)/pageBackgroundImage(...) and the /juneau-console/assets/logo/page-bg endpoints were removed; ConsoleChromeMixin.create().theme("<stock-name>") selects a stock palette for the served chrome.css. Page Tabs and Page Subtabs — a Page Tab is 38.5px tall: a 3px accent border, 8px/10px padding, and 13px text at line-height 1.5. A Page Subtab is 30px tall. The selected Page Tab and the selected Page Subtab are bold. The box is themeable through --jc-nav-tab-padding-block, --jc-nav-tab-padding-inline, --jc-nav-tab-line-height, --jc-page-nav-child-padding-block and --jc-page-nav-child-padding-inline. <@console theme="<stock-name>"> still selects a built-in stock theme (an unknown name is rejected fail-closed); a nested <@theme name=> inside the directive overrides it. The juneau-rest-server-theme-packs module was removed. juneau-console-freemarker — ConsoleFreemarkerMixin extends FreemarkerMixin (register it typed as FreemarkerMixin, mirroring the load-bearing-return-type rule FreemarkerMixin beans already follow) augments the resolved Configuration's TemplateLoader with a second, classpath-root-rooted ClassTemplateLoader, without shadowing the consumer's own basePath-relative templates. This resolves the reserved org/apache/juneau/console/base.ftlh template (pulled in via a loader-root-absolute <#include "/org/apache/juneau/console/base.ftlh">) and its <@tag domain=... value=.../> macro — the trusted-HTML adapter for the pill component above. A consumer-supplied Configuration bean (Spring Boot autoconfig, etc.) is honored untouched, not augmented. DataTablesTable additive @Html(render=...) honoring (in the existing juneau-console-datatables module) — DataTablesTable.of(MarshallingContext, String, Collection<?>, Class<?>) now resolves and applies each row property's @Html(render=...) the same way the ordinary HtmlSerializer/HtmlDocSerializer path already does, so a column whose bean property declares a custom @Html(render=...) (for example an enum rendered as a status pill) renders through it instead of as a raw enum name. This is not a purely-additive change: a bean already using @Html(render=...) for the existing serializer path now also renders through that same render when passed through this DataTablesTable overload, where it previously rendered the raw value. Map-based rows are unaffected (no BeanPropertyMeta to resolve a render from). juneau-console-freemarker — shareable-URL state and more datatables catalog keys. The views toolkit pack now includes juneau-urlstate.js (after juneau-pagestate.js), so the View Settings Copy link button and shareable-URL state work on <@page toolkit="views"> pages without loading the script by hand. <@card type="datatables"> catalogs now pass copyLink, rowActions, rowClassRules and pausePollingWhileEditing through onto the view, and selection and bulk through onto the slot; previously these keys were silently dropped on FTL-built pages. juneau-console-views / TableSpec — urlState key and the day(YYYY-MM-DD) directive. A table view can now opt in to built-in shareable-URL directives with TableSpec.urlState(String...) (or urlState: {day: {}} in a catalog; the page schema validates it). day stores a calendar date in ?state= and passes it to the server as a day query parameter (rename it with TableSpec.urlStateDayParam(String param), emitted as urlState.day.param) so a resource can return that day's [start, end) window; malformed dates are ignored. Views without the key are unchanged. juneau-console-freemarker — open card-type registry. Unknown well-formed card types now pass through the server, and the JS shell fails them with E-JS-4. <@card> gains a src= attribute. A bare-URL datatables body is removed (it is now E-25), and searchType validation moves to render time (E-32). The bulk wire contract is "2" (aggregate mode, BulkResult). <@card type="datatables"> is the one table surface. QuickStat gains meter and segmented kinds. QuickStat.meter(id, label, value, max) paints a filled track with role="meter", and QuickStat.segmented(id, label).segment(...) paints a proportional bar with a text legend. Both require a non-blank label. The new statusTone(StatusTone) sets an item tone from the shared status palette; tone(QuickStat.Tone) is unchanged. Inline datatables catalogs refuse a malformed quickStats strip (E-37). This includes an off-palette tone on any item, plain tiles included. Such tones used to be dropped silently by the client. See the new Admin-Console Chrome topic page.
documents.s: Themeable admin-console chrome + FreeMarker macro composition (new modules: juneau-console, juneau-console-freemarker)

documents.t: <@console> pages now carry a versioned JSON page contract (#juneau-page, schema juneau-page.schema.json) and load one shell script, /juneau-console/juneau-console.js, which draws the header, nav (any depth, aria-current from activeNav or a segment-aware URL fallback), cards and footer. The server keeps rendering <head>. New: PageContractAssert (published test helper), ConsoleTemplateValidator (static template lint), ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder.devMode(boolean) (schema validation at render time), jcHasToolkit(name), <@footer text="…"/>, and window.JuneauConsole (contract, card, registerCard, mount, chrome, and the juneau:console-mounted event). Loud failures: template mistakes fail the render with E-1 to E-18; contract problems in the browser show a .jc-console-error banner (E-JS-1 to E-JS-12, then E-JS-14). Fix: a @Bean returning ConsoleFreemarkerMixin (rather than FreemarkerMixin) is now found; previously it silently fell back to the default mixin without the console directives. BREAKING (10.0 snapshots only): the page contract's top-level version key is renamed contractVersion, matching every other Juneau envelope contract (ModalDef, FormDef, BarSlot, ActionResult, RegionDef, the card/slot envelopes). The value is unchanged ("1"). There is no fallback: juneau-page.schema.json now requires contractVersion and forbids version, juneau-console.js reads only contractVersion (JuneauConsole.SUPPORTED_VERSIONS is now SUPPORTED_CONTRACT_VERSIONS), PageContractAssert.hasVersion(String) is renamed hasContractVersion(String), and assertPage(...) throws if a contract still carries version. Pages are generated by <@console>, so upgrading Juneau is the only step; code that hand-builds a page contract, or calls hasVersion, must be updated. Browsers that cached the previous juneau-console.js (served with a one-day max-age) show an E-JS-2 banner until the cache expires or the page is hard-reloaded. BREAKING: the FTL globals pageBody, pageTab, pageInit, pageCss, pageToolkit, pageToolkitCss, pageToolkitJs and pageThemeCss are removed (use jcHasToolkit("views")). The legacy chrome templates that did not use <@console> are removed; a <@page> whose chrome renders no <@console> is an error. The <@card> types js, json and calendar are removed (use type="html" with a body or a registered card type), as are the data-juneau-card-sidecar scripts (no directive emits them any more; the orphaned juneau-page-cards.js asset is deleted). juneau-chrome.js is absorbed into juneau-console.js. Server HTML no longer contains nav, header, footer or card wrappers; tests that matched that HTML must move to PageContractAssert.
documents.s: Console page contract and JS shell

documents.t: Console cards now declare the scripts and stylesheets they need, and <@page> loads each one once, in dependency order. See Card Asset Dependencies. New: ToolkitPack (packs with dependsOn and a VENDOR / RUNTIME kind), the built-in packs jquery, datatables, datatables-glue and datatables-buttons, <@card requires=...>, and ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder methods registerToolkitPack(ToolkitPack), cardRequires(type, packs...) and providedPacks(names...). build() fails on an unknown pack, a cycle, or a VENDOR pack depending on a RUNTIME pack. New: <@card class="..."> adds one or more CSS classes to the card's wrapper element, so a page can keep its own scope class on the card. Each name must be a plain CSS class token or the render fails. See Admin Console Chrome. New: WebJarsMixin and WebJarResolver in juneau-rest-server serve /webjars/* from the classpath. juneau-console-datatables now depends on the jQuery and DataTables WebJars (DataTables 2.3.8, Buttons 3.2.6, jQuery 3.7.1). Changed: every <@card type="datatables"> loads jQuery, DataTables and juneau-datatables.js, in client and server mode. Previously the glue loaded only for server-mode cards and the page had to load jQuery and DataTables itself. A host with datatables cards composes WebJarsMixin as well as DataTablesMixin. BREAKING (10.0 snapshots only): juneau-datatables.js left the views pack. ToolkitPackRegistry.Resolved is split into vendorCss, vendorJs, runtimeCss and runtimeJs, and the resolve(names, req, boolean) overload is removed. A page that loads jQuery or DataTables through <@scripts phase="after-toolkit"> must drop those tags (they would load twice, after the glue). A copy loaded through init= or css= is skipped only when its file name matches the pack's; an app with its own copies should name the packs in providedPacks(...) or mount WebJarsMixin. Removed (10.0 snapshots only): APIs left unused once every consumer moved to card-declared packs. DataTablesMixin.JQUERY_CDN_URL, DATATABLES_JS_CDN_URL and DATATABLES_CSS_CDN_URL are gone; jQuery and DataTables now come from the WebJars. PageCapture.hasServerModeTable() is gone, because every datatables card now requires the datatables-glue pack. On ToolkitPackRegistry, the 2-arg resolve(names, req) and the register(name, cssPaths, jsPaths[, resolver]) overloads are gone; use resolve(names, req, pageUrls, template) and register(ToolkitPack). ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder.registerToolkitPack(name, cssPaths, jsPaths) and providedPacks(...) stay.

Juneau 10.0 replaces the multi-signal REST debug/logging system (@Rest(debug)/@Debug/DebugEnablement/ CallLogger) with a single, JUL-logger-level-driven mechanism. This is a hard break with no deprecation shim (unreleased 10.0 surface) — see the Breaking Changes section below and the V10 Migration Guide for the full removed-symbol mapping. One signal. A resource's own java.util.logging.Logger level is the sole control for request/response debug capture — no annotations, no per-request headers, no separate config keys. Verbosity is cumulative: INFO = basic, FINE = + headers, FINEST = + bodies (only when the body-dump gate is set — see the secure-by-default entry below), one LogRecord per request (stable emitted level: INFO). Per-operation granularity falls out of ordinary JUL parent-inheritance via a hierarchical child logger (resourceClass.getName() + "." + methodName) — elevate one method to FINEST without touching the rest. Off by default. Under stock JUL (nothing configured for the resource) no debug record is built or logged, so a running service no longer writes one line per request. The status line appears only when a level of INFO or finer is set explicitly on the resource's logger (or an enclosing logger such as its package), and FINE/FINEST add headers/bodies as before. The record is not constructed at all when it would not be emitted. Apps that relied on the per-request line appearing by default must now set the level, e.g. Logger.getLogger("com.acme.MyResource").setLevel(Level.INFO). Spring Boot propagation path. For real Logback backends, logging.level.* now propagates into JUL by default (juneau.rest.logging.propagate-levels=true), with an additive default posture (juneau.rest.logging.propagate-levels.reset-jul=false) and silent no-op fallback for non-Logback backends. New RestDebugFormatter SPI (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.logging) — a per-tier formatter interface (formatBasic/formatHeaders/formatBody) with a shipped BasicRestDebugFormatter default. It's the only public extension point; the two-phase capture pipeline underneath it is internal. Resolution precedence: resource-implements-the-interface > BeanStore-registered bean > BasicRestDebugFormatter. Secure by default (hardened). BasicRestDebugFormatter no longer dumps bodies just because a logger was raised to FINEST. See the dedicated secure-by-default entry below for the full contract. Bounded body buffering. Request/response body-caching wrappers are installed only when the resolved logger is loggable at FINEST, and buffer at most the configured cap rather than the entire stream — an improvement over the prior unbounded debug body caching. Completion-path emission for async/reactive responses. True asynchronous responses (CompletableFuture/CompletionStage) and reactive SSE/NDJSON streams now emit their single debug record on the response-completion path — after the async body and any completion-time headers have been written — instead of during the synchronous request finish. This fixes incomplete capture where an async record could be emitted before its late headers/body existed. A resolved logger/formatter/detail-tier snapshot is captured on the request thread at the async hand-off and carried across the completion hop; finish-time attributes such as Exec time are recorded on the completion path. Synchronous responses and the MockRestClient/non-async-container fallback are unchanged (still emitted during synchronous finish), and @RestEndCall still runs on the request thread. Exactly one INFO record is emitted per request on every path. Logger level controls verbosity only. REST-driven marshalling debug behavior and EchoMixin reachability are decoupled from the JUL level (see the dedicated entry below). RestRequest.isDebug() still exists, now derived and read-only (true when the resolved logger is FINE-or-finer), but the framework no longer keys any behavior off it. See the new Logging / Debugging topic page for the full model.

Two side effects that previously rode the JUL logger level are now controlled by their own explicit, non-logging switches — so raising a logger to FINE/FINEST changes verbosity only. This is an unreleased-10.0 hard break (no compatibility shim, no new echo annotation). EchoMixin is disabled by default. /echo/* now returns 404 Not Found regardless of logger level. Enable it explicitly: EchoMixin.create().enabled().build(). Enablement is tri-state — an explicit enabled(true)/ enabled(false) wins; when unset it resolves the ${juneau.echo.enabled:false} SVL fallback (system property / relaxed environment variable). Because that fallback is JVM-global, prefer per-host builder enablement and pair it with the host's inherited @Rest(guards=...) chain. This closes an accidental attack-surface expansion where raising a logger to FINE silently un-hid a request-reflecting endpoint. Marshalling debug behavior has a dedicated cascading setting. Serializer/parser debug behavior (richer/ stack-prefixed serialization exceptions and retained/quoted parse input in error messages) is now driven by debugMarshalling, a String on all eight REST annotation types (@Rest, @RestOp, and the six HTTP-method annotations) defaulting OFF at every level. Blank "" means inherit (op inherits resource, which resolves ${juneau.debugMarshalling:false}); query at runtime via RestRequest.isDebugMarshalling(). A serializer/parser configured with its own marshall-layer Context.debug remains independent — the REST layer never clobbers it. See Logging / Debugging and the Ops / Introspection Mixin Pack topic pages.
documents.s: Decoupled EchoMixin reachability and marshalling debug from log level

documents.t: BasicRestDebugFormatter is hardened so that raising a resource/operation logger to FINE/FINEST can never, by itself, leak plaintext credentials or hand a remote client a log-forging channel. This is an unreleased-10.0 hard break in the debug formatter's output — there is no compatibility shim. Two reusable primitives land in juneau-rest-common (a sanitize(...) log-forging escaper and the RestDebugBodyScrubber SPI); the formatter changes land in juneau-rest-server. No body dumps by default. Request/response bodies are never dumped unless an operator explicitly sets the JUNEAU_REST_DEBUG_ALLOW_DUMP_BODIES environment variable (environment-only, no system-property fallback, read once/cached, trim-then-parse truthy kill-switch semantics). With the gate unset, FINEST emits a suppression placeholder + byte count instead of body content. Even opted in, bodies render only at FINEST and only for renderable text content (via the new isBodyRenderable(String) predicate); non-renderable/binary content and non-identity Content-Encoding yield a distinct placeholder. RestDebugBodyScrubber SPI (org.apache.juneau.http) — an optional, gate-subordinate, fail-closed transform (String scrub(String contentType, String body), registered via bodyScrubber(...)) that chooses scrubbed-vs-raw body text once dumping is permitted; a throw or null result falls closed to a placeholder, never the raw body. All header values masked against a widened set. Every value of every credential-bearing header (not just the first) is masked with [REDACTED], using a widened formatter-local set (the shared RedactedHeaders.DEFAULT plus X-Auth-Token, X-Authorization, WWW-Authenticate, Referer, Location) matched with separator-normalized folding (so X-Auth-Token/X_Auth_Token/XAuthToken all match). RedactedHeaders.DEFAULT is unchanged. New additive addRedactedHeaders(...) knob alongside the replacing redactedHeaders(...). Log-forging sanitization. The request method/URI (including the 404/unrouted path), header names/values, and any dumped body text are escaped (CR/LF, NEL, line/paragraph/bidi separators, C0/C1 controls → \r/\n/\uXXXX; TAB preserved), so a client cannot inject a newline to forge a second log line or a fake status banner. Bounded output. New maxHeaders (100), maxHeaderScan (1000), maxFieldLength (1024), and maxUriLength (2048) knobs bound header and URI output; the existing bodyCap() remains the single body cap. Finish-path containment. A formatter or scrubber that throws during request completion can no longer escape and fail a completed request — only a fixed diagnostic token is logged (never the secret, message, or stack). See the Logging / Debugging topic page for the full model and the operator opt-in danger callout.

Juneau 10.0 adds always-on, end-to-end request correlation on the REST server. A per-request requestId is resolved during session build — before any @RestStartCall hook — so it covers every code path that produces a debug record, including 404s and early-error paths, and gives the debug formatter's statusLine a synchronous RestRequest.getRequestId() to read. Mint-or-honor. An inbound X-Request-Id request header is honored when present; otherwise a fresh time-ordered Uuid7 is minted. The resolved id is echoed on the X-Request-Id response header. Exactly one requestId LogContext scope is opened per request and closed after the debug record is emitted (emit-before-close), so every record on the request thread — the cumulative debug record and any handler-emitted records — carries the structured requestId field, and the rendered message is prefixed [requestId=<id>] . The id also rides the async-completion snapshot, so true-async completion records correlate identically. RequestIdSettings bean (public write-surface, resolved by RestContext via a getBean → @Bean-factory → default ladder): validator(Predicate<String>) defaults to sanitize-and-accept (strip log-forging sequences, accept the bounded remainder — not reject-and-remint), plus attributeKey(String) and idSupplier(Supplier<String>). RequestIdFilter reconciled to a thin façade. Its apply() is now idempotent with respect to the already-resolved session id (honor, never double-mint); its per-instance builder knobs are documented no-ops — request-id behavior is configured on RequestIdSettings. Auth non-influence. X-Request-Id has zero influence on authentication/authorization outcomes; configuring an auth guard to read it is an anti-pattern (regression-tested). See the Logging / Debugging topic page.

A new org.apache.juneau.commons.http.SafePathTemplate centralizes the same-origin/non-templated URL check and the MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5000 poll floor. The views toolkit's region and polling definitions call it, and the client-side runtime re-implements the same rule as defense-in-depth.

AsyncJobRegistry.tryCreate(IdempotencyKey) and create(IdempotencyKey) register a job under the key's value; submitting again with a key that is already registered returns the existing job instead of creating a second one, so a double-click, an impatient re-submit or a browser retry collapses to one job. Atomic. The lookup-or-create is atomic — concurrent submits with one key yield exactly one job. Finished jobs replay. A key whose job has finished returns that terminal job and its result (the same replay-on-duplicate contract as IdempotencyKey) rather than triggering a second run. This holds until the job is swept after the 60-second retention window; after that the key is forgotten and the same key starts a fresh job. Duplicates are free. A repeat request creates nothing, so it does not count against MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS.

Async job streams (/juneau-jobs/{jobId}/stream) now tag each progress event with an SSE id and resume from Last-Event-ID (or ?lastEventId=). A fresh attach no longer replays earlier progress. The job-log card asks for the full history itself. Live-only default (BREAKING). A fresh attach with no resume value no longer replays buffered progress. This affects every EventSource(streamUrl) client, including third-party callers of the HTTP API. Add ?lastEventId=0 to get the whole history. New lastEventId query parameter on GET /juneau-jobs/{jobId}/stream. A non-empty Last-Event-ID header beats it, so a browser's own reconnect resumes where it left off. 400 for a bad or past-the-end resume value. The status checks run in the order 404, then 400, then 429. An ended job still sends its result on every attach, fresh attaches included. Job-log card: connects with ?lastEventId=0 and no longer de-duplicates lines by count. See Async Jobs.
documents.s: Async job streams resume from Last-Event-ID (BREAKING)

documents.t: The View Settings dialog is reworked so that saved choices actually take effect on load. Applied on load. Stored View Settings (columns, search membership, sort, page size, wrap, density, auto-refresh) are restored when the page loads, not only when the dialog opens. This fixes a hidden column reappearing after a reload, in both client and server data modes. Ordered Sort tab. Sort is a priority list of column and direction entries, and an untouched Apply keeps the view's defaultOrder instead of persisting an ascending sort over every column. Auto-refresh. The Options tab gains an auto-refresh interval (Off, 30 s, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m), stored as autoRefreshMs. Per-view tabs. columnConfig: {tabs: [...]} restricts the dialog to a subset of columns, search, sort and options. Accessibility. Dialog tabs carry aria-selected/aria-controls with arrow-key navigation, every row control's label names its column, and a polite live region announces search results and a dismissed, unapplied search. Copy link button beside the gear, shown for the primary (or only) view table. Column search popover shows a per-type help line (the text of SearchType.bareHelp()). BREAKING: the columnSearchToggle ribbon type is removed. The ribbon ignores an unknown type silently, so an adopter just loses the button; per-column search is the search icon in each header cell. BREAKING: the saved View Settings schemaVersion is now 2, and NS.config.readViewSettings returns {settings, reset}. A saved blob at version 1, or with the old string-array sort, is discarded with a one-time notice; saved-view blobs at version 1 are rejected too. A stored blob is ignored for tables without columnConfig. BREAKING: NS.config.defaultSortMembership is removed. BREAKING: the Options blob gains autoRefreshMs (old blobs read as Off), and isPollSuspended now also returns true while the View Settings dialog is open, which pauses any existing pausePollingWhileEditing view. Layout refresh. The View Settings dialog gets a gear in its title, a Find... box and drag grips on the Available list, drag from Available into the selected grid, a detail strip fed by the new optional Column.description, a bordered Reset button and a compact saved-views row when no views are saved. See the new Datatable View Settings topic page.

New terminal-view region: a multi-step run summary driven by a small, versioned event stream, with <@card type="terminal-view">, TerminalViewMixin, and readers that turn test-report files into events. New module: juneau-terminal-report (package org.apache.juneau.terminal.report) holds TerminalEvent, the grammar checks (TerminalViewChecks) and the report readers. It does not depend on the REST server, so a producer can use it alone; juneau-console-views depends on it. Events: TerminalEvent factories for step, end, suite, test, replace, note and done (contractVersion "1"). The client reduces them to a failures-first summary, a step list, and per-suite strips of test blocks with tooltips; counts stay exact past the retention caps. Sources: TerminalViewLog (in memory) and FileTerminalViewSource (a growing JSON Lines file, with 410 Gone after truncation). Implement TerminalViewSource for anything else. Endpoint: TerminalViewMixin serves /juneau-terminal-view/{runId}/events; TerminalViewEndpoints gives the same logic for custom paths. Report readers: ReportReaders.forKind(...) reads Surefire, JUnit XML, pytest, Jest JSON and Playwright JSON reports without throwing on bad input, and ReportResult.toEvents(step) feeds the region. Re-run steps: steps named <id>.2, <id>.3 (titled (attempt N)) collapse under the latest attempt, behind an "N earlier attempts" toggle that starts collapsed. Client: juneau-terminal-view.js joins the views toolkit pack and publishes JuneauViews.terminalView. poll: false regions take events through append, so any transport (such as SSE) works. Errors: the region reports E-RV-1 to E-RV-9; the console shell adds E-JS-14. The console shell's unknown-card-type message now lists html|datatables|terminal-view. See the new Terminal View Region topic page.

New terminal region: a command's raw output rendered by xterm.js, colours, redraws and all, with <@card type="terminal">, TerminalMixin, and a launcher that runs commands under a PTY. New module: juneau-terminal-region (opt-in). It depends on juneau-console-views and the xterm.js WebJar org.webjars.npm:xterm__xterm 6.0.0. Endpoints: TerminalMixin serves /juneau-terminal/{id}/bytes (raw bytes by offset, with Term-* headers) and /raw; TerminalEndpoints gives the same logic for custom paths. Sources: FileTerminalSource (a growing log with a .size sidecar) and MemoryTerminalSource (a ring buffer). Launcher: TerminalProcess runs a command under juneau_terminal.py --pty and serves its log and events. juneau_terminal.py: new --pty, --size COLSxROWS and --events PATH options, plus --input stdin and --prompts stdio to pass input or the job's prompt channel through. Non-PTY runs are unchanged. Prompts: TerminalProcess.start(..., TerminalPrompts) relays the job's prompt lines and sends answers back with answer(jsonLine); closing it cancels the job. Terminal view: step, suite and test events gain an optional rawOffset; rawHref takes {offset} and onBlockClick gets offset. rawLine, {line} and info.line are gone. The contract version stays "1". Console UI: the terminal card type and the xterm and terminal toolkit packs. terminal is now a reserved card type name. It replaces the console-output card. xterm options: the client takes an allowlisted terminal object (convertEol, scrollback, fontFamily) in mount and on the terminal card; other keys are ignored. Server-built cards set it through the new TerminalDef.terminal(Map) builder method or the card body, and the server rejects unknown keys and bad values. See the new Terminal Region topic page.

New build tooling: juneau_terminal.py, a stdlib-only Python wrapper that runs Maven, pytest, Playwright, Gradle, npm and Bazel commands, parses their output into steps and test counts, and draws a board console view. Juneau's own test.py, push.py and release.py run on it. It is attached to org.apache.juneau:juneau-terminal as a py (the engine), a zip (bootstrap.py, the juneau_terminal_scripts toolkit, the pytest plugin and the Playwright reporter) and a py with classifier pytest. It is build tooling, so juneau-bom does not manage it. Console view: --console full|board|none (or JUNEAU_TERMINAL_CONSOLE), one row per step with a progress bar, counts and a summary line, and JUNEAU_TERMINAL_DETAIL (summary, actionable, modules, all) for how much a finished step keeps. --full-log and --board-log write the raw output and the rows. Run history: per-step timings and test counts under ~/.cache/juneau-terminal/history, shared by branches and worktrees of one repository, give percents, estimates and an Overall line (JUNEAU_TERMINAL_HISTORY, JUNEAU_TERMINAL_HISTORY_DIR, JUNEAU_TERMINAL_HISTORY_KEY). Run-protocol markers: TERMINAL_MARKERS=1 prints ##terminal <json> events for a runner UI, and TERMINAL_ARTIFACTS keeps copies of the test reports. Maven rows: one block per module. A single-project build (a one-module tree, or -pl without --also-make) draws one module and counts 1/1 on success. A build that stops before test (goals up to test-compile, or -DskipTests) still draws its module bar, counting modules as they compile, with no test totals. Pytest plugin: -p juneau_terminal_pytest is added to pytest runs (opt out with JUNEAU_TERMINAL_PYTEST_PLUGIN=0), so the bar has one block per test file and shows the running file. Without the plugin, the bar keeps one block per test. Playwright reporter: added through PW_TEST_REPORTER beside the config's reporters (opt out with JUNEAU_TERMINAL_PLAYWRIGHT_REPORTER=0). It gives one block per test file, counts a retried test once, writes <step>-playwright.json, and off a terminal sets PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never. PTY mode: --pty, --size, --events, --input stdin and --prompts stdio; this is what TerminalProcess runs (see the Terminal region section above). Cancelling: each tool runs in its own process group. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM sends SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL after a grace period, so forked JVMs and browsers don't outlive the run; the run ends as cancelled (exit 130). Script toolkit: juneau_terminal_scripts gives push and release scripts git helpers, a session with exit codes, tool runners, resumable steps, locks, notifications and prompts, loaded through the vendored bootstrap.py. Juneau build rows: test.py draws Compile, Java tests, Python tests and Browser tests (always shown, marked skipped with the reason when not run); push.py adds Prechecks, Tags, BOM, Timing, Install, Commit and Push. Wrapping: every line of a wrapped bar holds the same number of cells as the first. Expected tests: a running row shows the expected test total from previous runs, e.g. 41,200 / ~83,000 tests. Steadier estimates: the estimated total time changes only when a new estimate differs by more than 15 seconds or 10%, whichever is larger, and is rounded to 5, 15 or 30 seconds by size. The overall ~X left figure behaves the same way. See the new juneau-terminal topic page.

Two new console card types. Both load their script on demand through a toolkit pack, so pages that don't use them load nothing new. chart card: line, bar and donut charts drawn as inline SVG by juneau-charts.js, from a src= endpoint or inline data, with optional refreshMs, click-through, a data-table view and an open kind registry (JuneauCharts.register). Built from Java with the new ChartDef builder. job-log card: a form that starts an AsyncJobsMixin job, streams its progress lines, shows the outcome, offers Cancel, and reconnects after a reload. A dropped stream resumes after the last line shown, using the server's Last-Event-ID support (see "Async job streams resume from Last-Event-ID" above). Built from Java with CardSpec.of("job-log", id). Reserved: job-log is now a reserved card type. Chart data tab (BREAKING): the "Show data" button and toggle are removed. The new dataTab option (ChartDef.dataTab(), dataTab: true in JSON5, dataTab=true on the directive) adds Chart and Data folder tabs. A visually hidden data table is always present for screen readers unless a11y.table:false. Tabs turn compact automatically when the chart is nested in a switcher. Horizontal bar charts now show every category label and grow with the category count. Job-log: the submit button is a primary button, and the output pane stays collapsed until output arrives. See the new Chart Cards and Job-Log Card topic pages.

A job can now be started for one table row, from the row or from its detail panel, with a key the server binds to that row. JuneauViews.jobs: run (submit, stream from the start, settle, cancel, with onStart / onProgress / onResult / onEnd hooks and an optional paint: "none"), fetchKey, active, pending and cancel. It allows one job per row, takes the row id only from the row's stamp, and substitutes {id} only. "jobs" joins NS.HOOK_NAMESPACES. helpers.jobButton: a button that runs a row job through JuneauViews.jobs. JobKeyLedger and RowJobSubmit: server-side keys bound to an action, a row id and the caller, issued by a key endpoint, verified on submit, and spent once their job exists. A key for one row is refused for another with 409 write-guard:idempotency-binding-mismatch; a spent key replays its job or answers write-guard:idempotency-key-spent, so a replay never starts a second job. Job-log region: the job-log card now runs inside a row-detail region (populate: 'job-log', built from Java with JobLogRegion). It gains submit.envelope / submit.action, hidden fields, source: 'row.<field>' presets and output, which writes a result value into the card or panel. A datatables card with a job-log region loads the joblog pack by itself, through the new CardTypeHandler.requiredPacks(JsonMap). window.JuneauJobLog.mount mounts one programmatically. JobLogChecks holds the validation both paths share. New errors E-JS-109 to E-JS-113. A panel re-attached after a collapse can cancel its job. RegionDef.config: populator-owned configuration, emitted only when set and delivered to the populator as ctx.declared.config, including from a datatables card's detail.region. A busy row refuses ordinary row actions: a row action activated on a row that already has a pending or running job (a JuneauViews.jobs run or another row action's job) is refused with row-job-running and sends nothing, instead of starting a second concurrent job for the row. It runs normally once the job ends. Marker re-applied after redraws: a row's data-juneau-job marker, row-action jobs included, is put back on the new <tr> after every table draw, and cleared from whichever <tr> is drawn when the job ends. Poll held while a panel runs a job: while an expanded detail panel hosts a running row job, the table's timer reload is held and the staleness pill shows Paused, whether or not the view sets pausePollingWhileEditing. User reloads, sorts, filters and page changes still draw. Fix: in-panel elements resolve their parent row. hookContextOf, and with it NS.rowActions.contextOf, now resolves an element inside a detail panel to the panel's parent row and its data, instead of a child row with empty data. A row-detail region's visibleWhen therefore tests the parent row's data, as documented. An element in a nested table's own row still resolves that row. Fix: console-card detail regions project lazy. A datatables card's detail.region now carries the same lazy value as the builder path (false unless the region is a tab body), so the two produce the same sidecar. Petstore: the Jobs page gains a species table whose detail panel restocks that species, and a "Groom again" button on each groom run. See the new Row Jobs topic page and Job-Log Card.
documents.s: Row jobs and the row-aware job-log card (juneau-console-views, juneau-console)

documents.t: A table row can now expand into a tabbed detail panel with a header, header actions and one pane per tab. The wire contract stays at version "1"; every new key is additive, so a client that predates tabs paints the header only. RowDetail, DetailTab, RowDetailMixin: RowDetail.fromBean(...) serves a bean's readable properties from a lookup function; RowDetail.inline() paints from the row already in the table, with no request. DetailTab has four kinds: fields (a field grid, optionally in titled groups), table (a nested table scoped to the row), chart and client (a renderer registered in the browser). RowDetailMixin serves the detail, one tab and the tab counts under row-detail/{key}/{id}; every failure answers the same empty 404. Header actions: RowAction.link(id, urlTemplate) adds a same-origin navigation link beside the existing dialog and confirm-delete actions. A trash icon joins the sprite. Counts and labels: a tab's label can carry a server-side count (DetailTab.count(...)) or the nested table's row count (countFromRows()). Tabs can be hidden per row with visibleWhen. chart region type: RegionDef.chart(id, dataUrl) draws a line or bar chart from a region's own data URL, and a datatables card with a chart tab loads the charts pack by itself. JuneauCharts.mount(el, card, rows) draws a chart into any element. JuneauViews.detail.register(name, fn): registers a client tab renderer by name. Polling and redraws: a tab can refresh on every table poll (refreshOnPoll); a redraw re-opens the open rows with the same active tab. RowDetail.basePath(...) and the petstore: a bean-backed detail now serves under its owning resource (basePath("/console/pets") gives /console/pets/row-detail/pet/{id}), and a .ftlh catalog may carry a nested-table tab's contractVersion inside its nested slot. The petstore console adopts both: the Pets, Sold, Orders, Users and Store tables expand into bean-backed details with nested Orders, History and Pet tabs, and the Changes, Audit and pet History tables expand into inline details, in the Java page builders and the FreeMarker twins alike. A table can now declare rowIdField (TableSpec.rowIdField(...), or a rowIdField key in a .ftlh catalog) without enabling selection, so a tabbed detail works with no checkbox column; the Users table does this. The detail takes its row id from rowIdField, then the selection's, then a column named id or name, and a rowIdField that differs from the selection's is rejected. See Building a Console Page.

Three Java copies of logic that the views JS owns are removed, and the JS is the single implementation: CalendarLayout removed. Calendar lane and chip layout is computed by juneau-calendar.js only. CalendarDef and the calendar card are unchanged. RegionDef.serializeParams(...) / resolvedDataUrl() removed. Region data URLs are built client-side by juneau-regions.js. Saved views removed. SavedViewsMixin, SavedViewStore, InMemorySavedViewStore and SavedViewQuotaException are gone, along with the server persistence provider in juneau-config.js (createServerProvider, data-juneau-saved-views). Column configuration persists to localStorage only. Built-in operator help text moved to JS. Built-in SearchOperators no longer carry help on the wire. The column-search popover reads built-in help from JuneauViews.search.SearchOperators.help(name). Custom operators still supply their own help. Ribbon behavior: Client-mode tables now apply column-scoped ribbon options. Previously only server-mode tables did, so client-mode adopters needed their own bridge script. Ribbon values are BeanQuery $-expressions ($eq(DROPPED), $in(Waiting,"Partially reviewed")), never regular expressions. A regex-looking value is passed to the search engine as written and matches nothing useful. New default setting. Use default: true on an option, or default: '<memberId>' on an optionGroup, to choose the initial selection when nothing is persisted. A stored choice always wins. Nothing auto-selects without default. opt is no longer comma-joined across ribbon contributions. The last contribution wins. Parity corpus. ribbon-corpus.json (views test resources) is the contract between the JS encoder and the Java DataTables request decoder. RibbonCorpus_Test (Java) and RibbonCorpus_Parity_Test (JS) both bind to it. Any change to ribbon encoding must update the corpus in the same change. Migration: replace regex ribbon values with the equivalent $eq/$in. Replace any page script that auto-applied a ribbon's first option with default.
documents.s: Console views cleanup and ribbon parity corpus (BREAKING)

documents.t: RibbonItem.id(String): a ribbon item, including a refresh() item, can now carry an id. The id is emitted on the item's ribbon entry and is rejected on divider and export items. Ribbon optionGroup title: the group title is now rendered as role="group" with aria-label, so assistive technology announces it. No visible caption is drawn. Render.meta(String, Object): the value may now be a Number or Boolean, which stays a JSON number or boolean (for example meta("places", 2)). It was String-only. Column.href(...) implies render("linked"): a column with an href and no render now emits the linked renderer, in both Java (Column.toCatalogMap()) and FreeMarker (DatatablesCardType). An explicit render always wins. Migration: Column.toCatalogMap() used to throw IllegalArgumentException for an href without render("linked"). That throw is gone, so a test that expected it must change, and render("linked") may be dropped. RowDetail region is optional: RowDetail.toMap() no longer requires a region. A detail with none is a header-only panel whose title and icon are filled from the endpoint's fields, and its entry carries no region key. openConfirmOnlyDialog passes the row to a confirm renderer: a per-row action's confirmRenderer now receives rows (the one row), labelField and rowIdField, the same way the bulk path passes them, so it can name the row it guards. A ribbon-hosted dialog has no row, so rows is empty. Migration: a custom confirmRenderer that assumed rows was always empty or absent for a single-row action must handle a one-element rows. Same-origin path checks (stricter): a card src must be a relative or root-relative same-origin path, so an absolute https://this-host/... src is now rejected at page build. Same-origin path checks now reject a backslash anywhere (including in the query, for example /search?q=C:\x), a leading or trailing space or control character, any C0 control character, and DEL. Badge src and href must be same-origin paths. Migration: change an absolute card src to a root-relative path. PageSpec.card(...) runs the card type's handler (behaviour change): a builder-API card of an adopter (non-reserved) type is now built the way <@card> builds it. Its body map is the authored body, the type's registered CardTypeHandler validates it and returns the fragment the card carries, and an invalid body fails the render with the <@card> message. Markup passed to card(spec, markup) is the card's body, as the content of <@card> is: JSON5 markup is parsed by the handler and is not emitted as a <template>, its subscribes / publishes keys are wired onto the card (refused when the CardSpec sets them too), and markup is emitted as the card's template only when the handler captures it. As in <@card>, the body may not set a base key (id, type, title, src, template, ref), a card takes at most one of a body map, non-blank markup, template or src, and sanitize is refused before the handler runs. An unregistered type still passes its body through as-is. Previously such a card was seeded as written, with no validation, and its markup was always emitted as a template. Migration: a builder card that carried the handler's output (for example by calling toFragment itself) must carry the authored body instead.
documents.s: Console views API gap fixes (juneau-console-views, juneau-console-freemarker)

documents.t: Ribbons.standard(): a builder for the usual table ribbon (search, create, filters, export, copy link, collapse, columns, reset, refresh) with stable item ids; see the console views catalog. New item types: search, linkButton and columnSettings (Ribbons.search(), Ribbons.linkButton(), Ribbons.columnSettings()). New export canonical group: the canonical group order is now search, entity, filter, export, viewing, page, status (BREAKING for ribbons that relied on the old order). Icons: a Lucide icon sprite is bundled as the lowest icon layer (ISC and MIT licensed, see LICENSE) and is fetched on every console page. An option without an icon no longer falls back to tune; it uses an explicit icon, then a keyword hint, then its ordinal. collapseAll is hidden when the table has no row detail. resetDefaults is hidden when the table has no columnConfig. Hidden items leave no ribbon handle on the page. Ribbon claims, auto-mounts defer: a ribbon-hosted columns or link button replaces the table's own auto-mounted one.

New switcher card type: SwitcherDef, or <@card type="switcher"> with a JSON5 body, holds several views of the same data (for example a chart and a table) behind one tab strip. A view holds one card or a list of sections that each hold a card. Views are built on first selection and stay alive when hidden. State: the selected view and section are kept per card in the browser and written to the page address as sw(<id>:<view>[.<section>]). An address that names the switcher wins over the saved choice. See the Switcher Card topic. Rules: a nested card cannot be a switcher (E-JS-126), a nested card id must be unique on the page (E-JS-127), and a nested card publishes its card:<id> topic only once its view has been built. Petstore: the Store page shows its revenue, orders and pets charts in switchers, with a new /console/store/stats/revenue feed. Style: style is "tabs" (the default) or "slider". Slider polish: slider buttons no longer draw a stray border, hover is pill-shaped, and the thumb shadow comes from the new --jc-switcher-thumb-shadow token, which is none in dark mode. Stacked cards: SwitcherDef.View.cards(CardSpec...), or cards:[...] in JSON5, stacks several cards in one view. A view holds exactly one of card, sections or cards. Cards nested in a switcher render borderless inside the switcher's card.

Handles: every element of a console page (page, page tab, card, table, ribbon and ribbon item, row, row detail, detail tab, switcher, view, chart) has a handle in the browser, reachable with JuneauViews.model.get(path) and JuneauViews.model.page(). Handles carry refresh, setLabel, setBadge, show, hide, activate, emit, on, subscribe and publish. JuneauViews.tables.handle(el) now returns the model's Table handle. Named handlers: JuneauViews.handlers.register(name, fn) registers a handler, and the builders name it: Handled adds action, on and subscribe to CardSpec, TableSpec, RibbonItem, RowDetail, DetailTab and, for the loaded event, PageSpec. ModelAction and HandlerRef build the pieces. Built-ins: juneau.refresh, juneau.refreshClosest, juneau.expand, juneau.collapse, juneau.activate, juneau.publish, juneau.countLabel and juneau.countBadge. Pages with no Java: new JuneauViews.model.Page(...) and the other handle classes build a page in JavaScript, page.toJSON() returns the page contract, and JuneauViews.model.build(json, {root, document}) mounts hand-written JSON. JuneauViews.model.validate(json) checks it. The page contract gains modelVersion, scripts, allowInlineHandlers and a model block on elements. Page scripts: PageSpec.script(...) also lists the scripts in the contract, and the shell loads any that are not already on the page before it resolves handler names. Inline handlers: HandlerRef.inline(...) is off by default. PageSpec.allowInlineHandlers(true) loads juneau-model-inline.js and needs a Content-Security-Policy that allows 'unsafe-eval'; rendering fails with an IllegalStateException if the response CSP does not. Errors: E-JS-114 to E-JS-125 (handler names, unknown or throwing handlers, inline handlers, modelVersion, model findings, page scripts and a missing juneau-model.js). Cards are classes (BREAKING for custom card types): JuneauConsole.registerCard(type, Class) takes a class that extends JuneauViews.model.Card, with static roles and static ops maps. The object form registerCard(type, { render }) raises E-JS-21. The context object's members are now methods of the card, and cardApi(id) returns the card handle. The html, terminal-view, chart, terminal, datatables and job-log cards and the petstore cards were ported. Ribbon item ids: a ribbon item needs an id, because handlers and paths address it. Stock items default their id to the type name (linkButton to link, columnSettings to columns). A second item of the same type, or a custom type, needs an explicit id(...). Duplicate ids are rejected, and RibbonItem.action(id) rejects a null or blank id. See Client Object Model.
documents.s: Client object model, handlers and triggers (juneau-console, juneau-console-views, juneau-console-freemarker)

documents.t: Tab strips: the selected tab has an accent-wash fill (the new --jc-tab-selected-bg token, which defaults to --jc-accent-wash), bold text, a 3px accent top bar and an accent border. Unselected tabs are white. The tab row is shorter, and the panel below gets an accent border and padding. The solid accent fill of a selected tab is gone. One look everywhere: tab strips, row-detail subtabs and dialog sections share one folder-tab look, joined to its panel. This also fixes the clipped border on the selected tab. Card gap: stacked top-level cards are separated by the new --jc-card-gap token.

Symbols: symbol:<name> is accepted by <@console icon= favicon=> and for the header logo (HeaderSpec.logoSymbol, schema logo.symbol). The symbol is served from GET /juneau-symbol/<name>.svg. Date field: forms gain a date field type. Form contract version "3" (BREAKING): the dialog and form contract version is now "3" (FormDef and ModalDef CONTRACT_VERSION, and the JS runtime). Hand-written contract payloads that declare "2" are refused. Column search popover: the popover has Apply, Cancel and Clear buttons and no live preview. Apply, Enter and Clear commit the filter; Cancel, Esc and a click away leave it unchanged. TableSpec.columnSearchHelpUrl(String) (an http(s) or root-relative URL) adds a "?" help link. Column search help by type: a column with no search block now shows help for its inferred type (text, numeric, timestamp or boolean): a type line and plain-value help. The operators, examples and $and/$or/$not appear only after clicking the round "?" at the bottom right, in smaller text colored by the new --jc-search-help-fg token. The popover has a thin border, a small radius and the --jc-popover-shadow shadow, a bold title in the text color, 28px controls and normal-weight buttons. Inputs: a generic .jc-input class styles text inputs. Terminal: the new --jc-term-font-size token (default 12.5px) sets the terminal font size. A wide panel adds columns instead of enlarging the font; the font shrinks (down to 8px) only on narrow panels. Follow is now a toggle button (aria-pressed), and Search uses the console input styling.
documents.s: Console symbols, forms, column search and terminal polish (juneau-console, juneau-console-views, juneau-console-widgets, juneau-terminal-region)

documents.t: Detail views: fields lay out one per row, with the label on the left and the value on the right. The column count is still set with RowDetail.columns(int). Tables: body and header rows are tighter, including nested tables, and paging text is muted. The paging chevrons and the page-size drop-down caret are new thin original art. The bulk-selection line appears in its own row above the table toolbar, and only while rows are selected. Folder tabs: unselected tabs have a neutral top border. The selected tab fills with the new opaque --jc-tab-selected-bg token and covers the panel's top border, so it opens into the panel. Header logo classes (behavior change): .jc-logo is now only the tile. The default drop image moved to .jc-logo-default, which the console emits only when a logo has neither a symbol nor a src; image logos use .jc-logo-image and symbol logos .jc-logo-symbol (a white glyph on the accent tile). A symbol logo no longer sits on top of the drop. Pages that write class="jc-logo" by hand need jc-logo-default to keep the drop. Header logo: a page with a logo symbol but no juneau-icons.js now draws no logo, logs one console warning and still shows the text title. Logos on nested routes resolve correctly. Behavior change: load juneau-icons.js on any page that uses HeaderSpec.logoSymbol. View Settings dialog: sort rows have a fixed height, and columns are described as searchable unless they say otherwise. Behavior change: Apply now always closes the dialog on success. The save flow is one inline row: the view drop-down, Save, Save as... with an inline name field, Rename and Delete (disabled on built-in views such as Default). The ribbon button uses the settings gear; its columns id is unchanged. Saved views in the ribbon: a saved-views drop-down sits in the ribbon next to the gear, shown once a saved view exists. It marks "(modified)" when the table differs from the chosen view. The new table option savedViewsInRibbon (default true) turns it off. It is available in Java (TableSpec), FreeMarker and the JSON5 tableCatalog. Theme selector: an opt-in drop-down next to the auto/light/dark control, turned on with themeSelector=true on <@console> or PageSpec.themeSelector(true). "Page default" clears the pick. The pick is stored and applied before first paint. Behavior change: the juneau:theme-changed event detail now carries {scheme, theme}. Petstore: the Revenue KPI card is removed, the header shows the paw-print logo, the theme selector is on, and detail views use two or three columns. The running app seeds orders relative to today unless PETSTORE_FIXED_NOW is set, and the Pets, Orders, Users and Changes tables gain search metadata and operators.
documents.s: Console views polish: detail views, tables, saved views and themes (juneau-console, juneau-console-views, juneau-console-freemarker)

documents.t: The HTTP parameter annotations (@Header, @Query, @Path, @Content, @FormData, @Request, @Response, @StatusCode, @PathRemainder, @HasQuery, @HasFormData, @Contact, @License, @Tag) along with the constant classes (CollectionFormatType, FormatType, ParameterType) and the httppart.bean package (RequestBeanMeta, RequestBeanPropertyMeta, ResponseBeanMeta, ResponseBeanPropertyMeta, MethodInfoUtils) have been moved from juneau-marshall to juneau-rest-common. Package names are unchanged (org.apache.juneau.http.annotation, org.apache.juneau.httppart.bean), so import statements do not need updating. Maven resolves the classes from the new module location automatically. Existing compiled code will need recompilation. Removed Features​ serializer() and parser() attributes removed from @Query, @Header, @FormData, @Path, @PathRemainder, @Request, @Response. Use the new @HttpPartMarshalling annotation (in juneau-marshall) to specify custom HttpPartSerializer/HttpPartParser classes. @Repeatable removed from all HTTP annotations. Dynamic annotation stacking via on/onClass is no longer supported. on() and onClass() attributes removed from all HTTP annotations. @ContextApply removed from all HTTP annotations. 14 XAnnotation companion classes deleted (ContentAnnotation, FormDataAnnotation, HasFormDataAnnotation, HasQueryAnnotation, HeaderAnnotation, PathAnnotation, PathRemainderAnnotation, QueryAnnotation, RequestAnnotation, StatusCodeAnnotation). ContactAnnotation, LicenseAnnotation, TagAnnotation, and ResponseAnnotation remain for Swagger generation utilities. New @HttpPartMarshalling Annotation​ A new @HttpPartMarshalling annotation in juneau-marshall (org.apache.juneau.httppart) replaces the serializer() and parser() attributes that were removed from HTTP annotations. This decouples the HTTP annotations from HttpPartSerializer/HttpPartParser types. @HttpPartMarshalling(serializer=UonSerializer.class, parser=UonParser.class) @Query("name") String name

RestSharedConstants — Home for static literals shared across REST modules (server, client, mock) so wire names and similar strings stay aligned. Serializer/parser session option wire names are HEADER_JuneauSerializerOptions, HEADER_JuneauParserOptions, QUERY_juneauSerializerOptions, and QUERY_juneauParserOptions. Add more public static final fields when other cross-module constants are needed. (This supersedes the earlier RestSessionOptionWire type.)

A coordinated, breaking restructuring of the @Rest resource family establishes one consistent architecture across servlets, child resources, and mixins. All changes below are hard breaks with no deprecation bridges (acceptable for a new major version); they supersede the pre-rename class names used elsewhere in these notes. Naming triad — *Servlet / *Resource / *Mixin. Every reusable capability now follows a self-describing <Capability><Flavor> naming scheme, and the vestigial Basic prefix is dropped from capability classes (it is retained only on the convenience-bundle bases that have a barer sibling, e.g. BasicRestServlet): RestObject → RestResource (the non-HttpServlet child-resource base), cascading to BasicRestObject → BasicRestResource and BasicRestObjectGroup → BasicRestResourceGroup. The mixin pack drops Basic and standardizes on the Mixin suffix: BasicStaticFilesResource → StaticFilesMixin, BasicSwaggerResource → SwaggerMixin, BasicSwaggerUiResource → SwaggerUiMixin, BasicOpenApiResource → OpenApiMixin, BasicRedocResource → RedocMixin, BasicRouteIndexResource → RouteIndexMixin, BasicEchoResource → EchoMixin, BasicAdminResource → AdminMixin, BasicVersionResource → VersionMixin, BasicWellKnownResource → WellKnownMixin, BasicSeoResource → SeoMixin, BasicFaviconResource → FaviconMixin, and the four view mixins BasicJspResource/BasicMustacheResource/BasicThymeleafResource/BasicFreemarkerResource → JspMixin/MustacheMixin/ThymeleafMixin/FreemarkerMixin. The servlet companions drop Basic too: BasicStaticFilesServlet → StaticFilesServlet, BasicAdminServlet → AdminServlet, BasicVersionServlet → VersionServlet, and the abstract BasicViewServlet → ViewServlet (with Basic*Servlet view companions → <Engine>Servlet). New RestMixin base (opt-in). A third base class org.apache.juneau.rest.servlet.RestMixin joins RestServlet and RestResource to complete the triad. It is opt-in — a plain @Rest POJO remains fully valid as a mixin or child via annotation-only configuration; extending RestMixin is a convenience and does not change composition semantics. Beyond the fluent builder surface it shares with RestServlet / RestResource (see the builder-API entry below), RestMixin adds getHostContext(), which returns the host (mixed-into) resource's RestContext — backed by the mixin sub-context's parent linkage, so it is usable at config time and does not depend on an in-flight request — letting a mixin op introspect the host (e.g. enumerate the host's child resources for a navigation page) rather than its own childless sub-context. It returns null when a RestMixin subclass is instantiated standalone rather than composed via @Rest(mixins=...). Op-interfaces deleted; replaced by single-responsibility op-mixins. BasicRestOperations and BasicGroupOperations are removed. Their endpoints are now true @Rest(mixins=...) mixins — ErrorMixin (/error), HtdocMixin (/htdoc), StatsMixin (/stats), and FaviconMixin (/favicon.ico) — added to the @Rest(mixins=...) lists of BasicRestServlet / BasicRestResource and the Spring BasicSpringRestServlet. The host-wide nav-links / JSON-schema configuration that lived on BasicRestOperations is re-homed as class-level @HtmlDocConfig / @JsonSchemaConfig on BasicRestServlet; the per-method @HtmlDocConfig page decoration moves onto StatsMixin.getStats (OQ-8). getChildren stays a concrete method on the group bases (BasicRestServletGroup / BasicRestResourceGroup / BasicSpringRestServletGroup) so the host's main navigation page retains its @HtmlDocConfig chrome (a mixin op runs in its own sub-context and would lose the host's page decoration). Favicon reconciliation. The legacy getFavIcon op (which served REST/favicon → images/juneau.png through static files) is dropped in favor of a FaviconProvider-backed flavor set: the flavor-neutral FaviconProvider worker bean holds the icon bytes + Cache-Control value and the serve logic, and the independent FaviconMixin (mixin) / FaviconResource (child) / FaviconServlet (servlet) flavors each hold a FaviconProvider and delegate to it. The default serves a classpath ICO (/juneau-favicon.ico) with a 30-day Cache-Control (max-age=2592000, public). This is a behavior change for both the default favicon bytes and the configuration key. Per-capability flavor fill-in (flavor-neutral worker beans). Capabilities where standalone or routed-child deployment is a real use case gain their missing flavors as independent classes that each delegate to a flavor-neutral worker bean — never to another flavor — so the forms cannot drift. The new worker beans are FaviconProvider / VersionProvider (in rest.convention), AdminProvider (in rest.ops), HealthAggregator (in rest.health), and the four view-engine raw-template dispatchers JspDispatcher / MustacheDispatcher / ThymeleafDispatcher / FreemarkerDispatcher; the static-files flavors resolve the existing StaticFiles worker bean from the request context (RestContext.getStaticFiles()) instead of holding a mixin instance. New child-resource flavors: StaticFilesResource, VersionResource, AdminResource, HealthResource, plus a ViewResource abstract base and per-engine JspResource / MustacheResource / ThymeleafResource / FreemarkerResource; new favicon flavors FaviconServlet and FaviconResource. HealthServlet / HealthMixin / HealthResource all delegate to a shared HealthAggregator (OQ-5 split of the former HealthServlet). All other capabilities (Swagger, SwaggerUi, OpenApi, Redoc, RouteIndex, Error, Stats, Htdoc, WellKnown, Seo) remain mixin-only. RestRequest.getStaticFiles() removed. The request-level forwarder is deleted; obtain the active StaticFiles bean via RestContext.getStaticFiles() (e.g. req.getContext().getStaticFiles()) or bean-store injection. FileVar, Widget, and the static-files flavors are repointed accordingly. RestContext.getStaticFiles() is unchanged. Route-index endpoint now content-negotiated. RouteIndexMixin (/options) returns a RouteDescriptions POJO instead of writing JSON directly, so the listing is now content-negotiated through the host's configured serializers: Accept: text/html renders a browsable table with clickable route links, while application/json / text/xml clients receive the same entries in their requested format (mirroring NavigationMixin.getChildren(...)). Because it now relies on the host's serializers, the host must have serializers configured (e.g. via BasicUniversalConfig or a Basic* servlet base) — a bare @Rest host with no serializers can no longer content-negotiate the listing, whereas the former JSON-only op did not require them. The historical /routes alias remains reachable via -Djuneau.routeindex.path=routes.
documents.s: REST class family architecture — naming triad, RestMixin, op-mixins, flavor fill-in

documents.t: A public, fluent builder surface lets a @Rest resource, child resource, or mixin be configured programmatically — the primary use case being instantiating a configured resource bean in a Spring @Bean method — instead of (or layered over) the @Rest annotation. Builder-supplied values take precedence over the class's own @Rest annotation members. RestBuilder<SELF> config surface + AbstractRestBuilder<R, SELF> base (full self-type CRTP). The public interface org.apache.juneau.rest.RestBuilder<SELF extends RestBuilder<SELF>> declares one fluent setter per @Rest member, plus the programmatic-only mdcAsyncPropagation(boolean) knob and a set(String, Object) forward-compat escape hatch. The shared abstract base AbstractRestBuilder<R, SELF extends AbstractRestBuilder<R, SELF>> implements every setter once — recording into a backing RestAnnotation.Builder override bag and returning self() — and leaves the SELF self-type open so a builder subclass's bespoke setters chain with true covariant returns (Option B / CRTP, aligned with the project-wide SELF / self() convention). Per-flavor builders with a concrete DefaultBuilder<R> leaf. Each base class exposes its own self-typed flavor builder — RestServlet.Builder<R, SELF>, RestResource.Builder<R, SELF>, and RestMixin.Builder<R, SELF> — together with a concrete DefaultBuilder<R> leaf. The static factory RestServlet.builder(MyRest.class) (and the RestResource / RestMixin equivalents) returns the DefaultBuilder<R>, so the common, non-subclassed path never has to spell two type parameters: @Bean public MyRest myRest() { return RestServlet.builder(MyRest.class) .path("/foo") .allowedHeaderParams("foo") .build(); } A resource may also add a one-line static Builder<MyRest> builder() { return RestServlet.builder(MyRest.class); } sugar so callers can write MyRest.builder().path("/foo")....build(). Constructor trio + builder-beats-annotation precedence. Every family base provides the constructor trio: a no-arg constructor, a Foo(RestBuilder) builder-injection constructor, and a Foo.Builder. build() stashes the builder onto the produced instance (a package-private restBuilder field read non-reflectively via getRestBuilder()). At RestContext construction the stashed builder's override bag is turned into a synthetic @Rest annotation prepended as the most-derived entry of the resource's annotation chain, so builder-set values win over the class's own @Rest members (rung 1 of the existing override-resolution chain). Collection-valued members replace the annotation value rather than merging. Mirror-and-forward builders for worker-backed capabilities (OQ-11). For a multi-flavor capability whose logic lives in a flavor-neutral worker bean, the flavor builder mirrors the worker bean's builder methods on its own surface and forwards into the worker's builder, while inheriting the full RestBuilder surface from RestMixin.Builder. For example FaviconMixin.create() mirrors bytes / classpath / cacheControl into FaviconProvider.Builder and inherits path / roleGuard / etc.; VersionMixin mirrors VersionProvider the same way. This is how the three flavors share capability config without a shared flavor-builder base class (Java single inheritance forbids one — each flavor builder already extends its REST builder base): @Bean FaviconMixin favicon() { return FaviconMixin.create() .classpath("/myapp/icon.ico") // mirrored → FaviconProvider.Builder .path("/branding") // inherited RestBuilder surface .build(); } Bean-instantiation preference (internal). So the new generic builder(Class) factories don't hijack framework default instantiation, BeanInstantiator now prefers a builder that builds the exact requested type (or a usable direct constructor) over one that only promises a supertype. A flavor's own create() / nested Builder therefore wins over the inherited generic builder(Class) (whose build() erases to a base class), and a plain resource/mixin carrying only the inherited builder falls through to its no-arg constructor.
documents.s: Fluent programmatic builder API — RestBuilder / AbstractRestBuilder self-type CRTP

documents.t: Parent resources annotated with @Rest(lazyChildren=true) now defer the construction of each child RestContext until the first HTTP request routed to that child. Default behavior (eager at startup) is unchanged for all existing code. @Rest(lazyChildren="true") on the parent resource opts all declared @Rest(children=...) into deferred (first-invocation) construction. The value is a String member with full SVL variable support (e.g. @Rest(lazyChildren="${E:LAZY_CHILDREN:false}")). RestContext.Builder.lazyChildInit(boolean) is the host-wide programmatic knob with the highest resolution priority (overrides both annotation and ${RestContext.lazyChildren:false} env default). Shell-context routing: At parent startup the route table is fully populated — each lazy child contributes its path prefix (resolved from @Rest(path=...) without instantiating a full context) to the parent's RestChildren matcher list. URL matching works immediately; the full RestContext is built only on the first matching request. Concurrency safety: Exactly one materialization per child even under concurrent first-requests. RestChildren.LazyChildEntry.materialize() uses a double-checked lock on a per-entry Object lock with a volatile RestContext materialized field. Two simultaneous first-requests serialize on the lock; the second thread reads the already-built context without re-constructing. A materialization that throws leaves the materialized field null — the next request retries. Observability: Materialization is logged at INFO level: Lazy REST child materializing: com.example.ChildResource at path '/child' / materialized. Lifecycle: RestContext.destroy() (via RestChildren.destroy()) only calls the child's shutdown hooks if the child was actually materialized. Never-invoked children are silently skipped. Interaction with @Rest(observability="true"): Startup-fail is also deferred — the observability-backend wiring check fires when the lazy child is first materialized, not at parent startup. @Rest(path="/api", children={AdminResource.class, MonitorResource.class}, lazyChildren="true") public class ApiGroupResource extends BasicRestServletGroup { // AdminResource and MonitorResource are built only on first request }

When a non-no-op TracerHook is active on a request, the server now writes the W3C traceparent — and, when present, the tracestate — header back onto the HTTP response, so a client calling the server can read the resulting trace id off the response and correlate against it. The emitted traceparent reflects the server-started span's context (a freshly-minted span id parented to the inbound trace), not the inbound header verbatim. tracestate is written only when the active trace state is non-empty — an empty trace state never produces an empty header. org.apache.juneau.rest.server.tracing.TraceContextResponseProcessor (new) — a ResponseProcessor prepended to the default ResponseProcessorList. It reads the rendered traceparent / tracestate strings that a TracerHook bridge stashed as request attributes (juneau.traceparent / juneau.tracestate) and writes them as response headers. Its first action is a single request-attribute read that short-circuits with zero allocations when no tracer ran, preserving the off-by-default observability contract on the no-tracer path. If the response is already committed (e.g. a streaming / SSE handler that flushed headers early) it logs a FINE message and skips the write — it never throws. The processor carries no OpenTelemetry dependency, so core juneau-rest-server stays OTel-agnostic; it works with any TracerHook bridge that populates the two attributes. RestContext.responseTraceparent (new env-driven default, ${RestContext.responseTraceparent:true}) — controls whether TraceContextResponseProcessor is registered.
